title: Papyrus: declare Biblicus dependency and replace subprocess bridges with one runner
description:
## Goal (Papyrus repo, AnthusAI/Papyrus; tracked here because it depends on a Biblicus release)
Replace four hand-written subprocess bridges and the sibling-checkout assumption with one declared dependency and one runner.

## Findings
- Papyrus declares no Biblicus dependency. `uv.lock` pins biblicus 1.11.1 only through `tactus @ file:///Users/ryan/Projects/Tactus`.
- `BIBLICUS_ROOT` defaults to `../Biblicus`; `analysis_profiles.py` hardcodes `/Users/ryan/Projects/Biblicus`.
- Four modules each build their own subprocess: `newsroom.py` (`.venv/bin/python -m biblicus`), `reference_url_text.py` and `reference_curation_signals.py` (same, plus `PYTHONPATH=BIBLICUS_ROOT/src`), `curation_cycle.py` and `accession.py` (`uv run --extra topic-modeling biblicus`).
- `reference_url_text.py` retries under `uv run --extra markitdown` when MarkItDown is missing.

## Work (after the curation surface is released)
1. Declare `biblicus[web,ner,markitdown,topic-modeling,openai]>=<release with curation commands>` directly in `pyproject.toml`.
2. One `BiblicusRunner` class owns the subprocess: executable resolution, environment, JSON parse, typed errors. Keep the process boundary; it keeps BERTopic and spaCy out of the Lambda runtime.
3. Remove every `/Users/ryan` default; take `BIBLICUS_WORKDIR` from the environment or fail with a clear message.
4. Add Papyrus CI that runs its Python tests against the released Biblicus.
